description: Analyst-reviewed overrides for identities that automatic corpus census materialization cannot classify safely by name/origin alone.

identity_boundaries.reason: Mandiant states that FIN11 contains only a subset of activity called TA505 and explicitly cautions against using the names interchangeably.
MITRE ATT&CK tracks TA505 as G0092 and Indrik Spider/Evil Corp as separate Group G0119.
Microsoft's current official mapping tracks Spandex Tempest with TA505 and tracks Lace Tempest separately with DEV-0950.
GTIG tracks FIN11 as RAZOR COMET while Microsoft's current official mapping tracks Lace Tempest with DEV-0950; neither primary mapping makes the names interchangeable.
Mandiant states that APT38 activity is disparate from TEMP.Hermit despite shared resources.
MITRE ATT&CK tracks Naikon (G0019) and APT30 (G0013) separately and says they share characteristics but are not exact matches.
MITRE ATT&CK tracks Dragonfly (G0035) and ALLANITE (G1000) separately; ALLANITE has similar tactics but a distinct observed capability boundary.
MITRE ATT&CK 19.2 tracks Lotus Blossom (G0030) and Thrip (G0076) as separate Groups even though Thrip also appears in Lotus Blossom's associated-name set.
MITRE ATT&CK 19.2 tracks Mustang Panda (G0129) and LuminousMoth (G1014) separately and describes only targeting, TTP, and infrastructure overlap.
MITRE ATT&CK 19.2 tracks Ember Bear (G1003) and Saint Bear (G1031) separately and explicitly states that behavior, tooling, and targeting distinguish the clusters despite prior confusion.

reference_identities.source: Google Threat Intelligence Group unified actor naming
Google Threat Intelligence Group unified actor naming

ta505.reason: FIN11, Indrik Spider/Evil Corp, and Lace Tempest are removed from TA505 using Mandiant, MITRE, and Microsoft's current primary mappings.

fin11.reason: Mandiant tracks FIN11 separately from TA505; GTIG renamed FIN11 to RAZOR COMET in July 2026.

indrikspider.reason: MITRE ATT&CK defines Indrik Spider/Evil Corp as Group G0119, separate from TA505 G0092.

lacetempest.reason: Microsoft's current official mapping tracks Lace Tempest with DEV-0950 in a separate row from Spandex Tempest/TA505.

apt38.reason: TEMP.Hermit is removed because Mandiant explicitly separates it from APT38 despite shared resources.

temphermit.reason: Mandiant tracks TEMP.Hermit separately from APT38; GTIG renamed TEMP.Hermit to HERMIT NEPTUNE in July 2026.

naikon.reason: APT30 is removed because ATT&CK tracks the groups separately and says they are not exact matches. GTIG maps Naikon Team to NAIKON CASTLE.

apt30.reason: ATT&CK tracks APT30 separately from Naikon; GTIG renamed APT30 to ISTHMUS CASTLE.

dragonfly.reason: ALLANITE is removed because ATT&CK ICS tracks it as separate Group G1000 with similar TTPs but a distinct capability boundary.

allanite.reason: MITRE ICS ATT&CK defines ALLANITE as Group G1000 and lists Palmetto Fusion as its associated group name.

cyberav3ngers.reason: MITRE ICS ATT&CK defines CyberAv3ngers as G1027. The joint CISA advisory explicitly lists the additional private-industry and open-source names, including UNC5691.

unc5691.reason: The corpus's joint CISA advisory explicitly identifies UNC5691 as another name used for CyberAv3ngers.

storm0784.reason: The corpus's joint CISA advisory explicitly identifies Storm-0784 as another name used for CyberAv3ngers.

radiopanda.reason: The joint U.S.-Japan cybersecurity advisory explicitly identifies Radio Panda as another name for BlackTech.

revil.reason: REvil is a ransomware/RaaS software-brand entity in this corpus context. MITRE ATT&CK tracks REvil as Software S0496 and tracks GOLD SOUTHFIELD (G0115) as the financially motivated group that operates the REvil RaaS. Do not materialize REvil as an independent canonical actor from name mentions alone.

whitecompany.reason: The census identity 'White Company' and the existing 'The White Company' profile refer to Operation Shaheen and the same Pakistan government/military targeting. MITRE ATT&CK canonicalizes this actor as The White Company (G0089).

carberb.reason: The corpus spelling 'Carberb' is retained only as a legacy alias. Group-IB identifies the Carberp hacking group as financially motivated and distinguishes the group from the Carberp banking Trojan used by multiple criminal groups.

fin8.reason: MITRE ATT&CK explicitly describes FIN8 (G0061) as a financially motivated threat group; workbook placement in the Russia worksheet is not sponsorship evidence.

blackbyte.reason: MITRE ATT&CK describes BlackByte (G1043) as a ransomware threat actor. The corpus-derived names Black Basta, Conti, DEV-0569, Diavol, Quantum, Royal, Ryuk/FIN12 and Wizard Spider are separate actors/groups and must not be aliases of BlackByte.

gravityrat.reason: GravityRAT is malware, not a canonical threat actor. MITRE ATT&CK tracks GravityRAT as Software S0237. ESET tracks the actor behind GravityRAT as SpaceCobra while noting the actor's real identity remains unknown.

shamoon.reason: Shamoon is wiper malware (MITRE ATT&CK Software S0140). Although the name is sometimes used colloquially for operators, actor identity must be modeled separately. CrowdStrike tracks VOLATILE KITTEN as an Iran-based actor/development team associated with Shamoon, and ETDA groups Greenbug/Volatile Kitten.

calypso.reason: ETDA Threat Group Cards maps Calypso (Positive Technologies) and Bronze Medley (SecureWorks) to the same tracked group. Comment Crew/APT1 and other workbook-derived cluster names are not Calypso aliases.

greenbug.reason: CrowdStrike tracks VOLATILE KITTEN as an Iran-based state-sponsored adversary associated with Shamoon, while ETDA maps Greenbug and Volatile Kitten together as an OilRig subgroup. Because the vendor-name boundary remains overlapping rather than exact, Greenbug keeps a neutral threat-cluster type and records state alignment separately.

syrianelectronicarmysea.reason: CrowdStrike previously tracked the Syrian Electronic Army as DEADEYE JACKAL and later renamed that Syria-nexus tracking to DEADEYE HAWK. Both names remain scoped aliases rather than automatic exact identities because vendor collection boundaries can differ.

earthberberoka.reason: Trend Micro introduced Earth Berberoka as the same tracked activity it calls GamblingPuppet. The spaced workbook variant duplicates that vendor name after normalization and is removed.

foxkitten.reason: MITRE ATT&CK supplies the retained associated names. ClearSky describes Pay2Key as an operation conducted by Fox Kitten, not as an actor alias. The punctuated PioneerKitten workbook value duplicates Pioneer Kitten after normalization.

ke3chang.reason: MITRE ATT&CK supplies the retained associated names, and Unit 42 explicitly maps Playful Taurus and BackdoorDiplomacy to APT15/Ke3chang while vendor collection boundaries remain overlapping. Uncorroborated workbook-only names and the normalized duplicate Royal APT are removed.

peachsandstorm.reason: MITRE ATT&CK tracks Peach Sandstorm as an associated name of APT33 under the same Group G0064. Maintaining both as active canonical actors duplicates the same vendor-renamed group.

raspberrytyphoon.reason: MITRE ATT&CK tracks Raspberry Typhoon as an associated name of Lotus Blossom under the same Group G0030. The Microsoft name must not be materialized as a second canonical actor.

sangriatempest.reason: MITRE ATT&CK tracks Sangria Tempest as an associated name of FIN7 under the same Group G0046. The Microsoft name must remain an alias of FIN7 rather than a separate active actor.

violettyphoon.reason: MITRE ATT&CK tracks Violet Typhoon and APT31 as associated names of ZIRCONIUM under the same Group G0128. The Microsoft name must not be materialized as a second canonical actor.

shinyhunters.reason: MITRE ATT&CK 19.2 assigns ShinyHunters/Bling Libra to Group G1057, while the repository already uses the stable UNC6240 profile and Microsoft's official mapping links Storm-3127 to UNC6240. Preserve the stable profile rather than creating a duplicate ShinyHunters actor.

barium.reason: MITRE ATT&CK tracks BARIUM as an associated name of APT41 under Group G0096; the standalone BARIUM profile contains no distinct activity and duplicates the canonical APT41 entity.

vicesociety.reason: Microsoft states that DEV-0832 is also known as Vice Society and that DEV-0832 is now tracked as Vanilla Tempest. The legacy Vice Society profile therefore duplicates Microsoft's canonical Vanilla Tempest entity.

judgementpanda.reason: The joint CERT-EU/ENISA publication explicitly identifies APT31 as also known as Judgment Panda and Zirconium. The legacy Judgement Panda profile is therefore an exact-identity duplicate of the ZIRCONIUM/APT31 profile.

uac0010.reason: Ukraine's State Cyber Protection Centre explicitly identifies the Russian-sponsored UAC-0010 group as also known as Gamaredon and Armageddon. The standalone UAC-0010 profile therefore duplicates the Gamaredon profile.

zebrocy.reason: Zebrocy is a malware family/toolset used by APT28/Sednit, not an independent canonical actor. MITRE ATT&CK tracks it as Software S0251, and ESET describes Zebrocy as downloaders, droppers, and backdoors operated by the Sednit group.
